# TugQL

> TugQL is an open, portable, human-readable query language and structured query tree (TugQT) for relational, document, API, and graph-connected data. The language specification is published in the public repository: https://github.com/tugql/tugql

TugQL (formerly DTQL) pairs an SQL-like text syntax with TugQT, a structured query tree serialized as YAML or JSON. A query is written once and runs across Git, SQLite, PostgreSQL, and Firestore. This website, https://tugql.org, is the canonical public introduction and is published in several languages. It is not the language specification. dtql.org is the former name and is kept as a permanent redirect to https://tugql.org.

The specification repository is licensed under the [Apache License, Version 2.0](https://github.com/tugql/tugql/blob/main/LICENSE).

## Specification

- [TugQL repository](https://github.com/tugql/tugql): Language specification, canonical JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), and reference documents.
- [Licence](https://github.com/tugql/tugql/blob/main/LICENSE): Apache License, Version 2.0, for the specification repository.
- [README](https://github.com/tugql/tugql/blob/main/README.md): Project definition, naming, and links to the reference documents.
- [Comments](https://github.com/tugql/tugql/blob/main/reference/comments.md): Comment syntax for the text form and the YAML form.
- [Negative projection](https://github.com/tugql/tugql/blob/main/reference/negative-projection.md): Selecting all columns except an explicit list.
- [Aggregation](https://github.com/tugql/tugql/blob/main/reference/aggregation.md): Grouping, aggregate expressions, and HAVING in the specification.

## Implementations

- [Go library](https://github.com/dal-go/dalgo/tree/main/tugql): Parse, validate, resolve, format, and execute TugQL queries.

## Optional

- [DataTug](https://datatug.app): Product whose query-contract work around TugQL and TugQT is ongoing.
- [DataTug query tools](https://datatug.app/en/under-the-hood/tools-we-built/#query): Notes on the tools behind that work.

## About the technology

The site uses a Node.js static HTML generator and Cloudflare Workers Static Assets. The open language specification is at https://github.com/tugql/tugql; its Go implementation lives in DALgo at https://github.com/dal-go/dalgo/tree/main/tugql.
